title: t2 (null-random-init): the loaded checkpoint does not perform the behaviour
label: no behaviour - nothing to explain
behavior: BOS + 5 tokens from 6 symbols -> one symbol at the last position (glassbox-bench seed-1 task t2). Asked: recover the function and the heads/MLPs implementing it.
summary: Negative result. On local-full (full precision) the loaded checkpoint agrees with the dataset's answers at chance level: 17.5% on 200 prompts (E0002) and 12.25% on 400 fresh prompts (E0003), against 16.7% chance for 6 symbols. The mean logit difference between the labelled answer and the foil is ~0 (-0.009 and -0.029, std ~0.23) and is no larger on clean than on corrupt prompts. The model therefore does not compute the function the labels encode, and the investigation was stopped at step 1 as the protocol requires. No function, no circuit and no predict() are claimed for this model; verify_hypothesis was deliberately not run.

claims.text: The loaded checkpoint does not produce the dataset's answers: argmax agreement is 17.5% on 200 prompts, at chance (16.7%), with mean logit diff -0.009 +/- 0.229 (local-full, full precision). My pre-registered prediction of >=98% was refuted.

The chance-level result replicates on an independent sample: 12.25% agreement on 400 prompts (seed 2), mean logit diff -0.029 +/- 0.223, below both the 30% threshold and the ~60% a majority-label predictor would reach (local-full).
Because the behaviour is absent, no attention head or MLP layer can be said to implement it; no circuit is claimed.

limitations: Only the baseline was measured (3 of 25 experiments used); no component-level experiments were run because there is no behaviour to attribute.

The task statement says the dataset's answers are the model's own outputs; that is not true of the checkpoint as loaded here. I did not determine why (the investigation name suggests a null control with re-initialised weights, but that was not measured).

Side observation, not a claim about this model: in the 64 labels inspected in E0001 (exploratory) the answers are consistent with a fixed priority rule bo > nu > pa > la > {ri, vu} (output the highest-priority symbol present). This describes the labels only, is unverified beyond those 64 examples, and the ri/vu order was not observed.
open_questions: Is this checkpoint an intentional null (random-init) variant of the t2 model, with labels taken from the original?
Does the original t2 model implement the priority rule suggested by the labels?
overall_status: unverified (no verification run) · no behaviour - nothing to explain

refuted_predictions.hypothesis: The model deterministically does the behaviour: on the bench dataset its top output at the last position equals the recorded answer (the dataset's answers are its own outputs), with a clear logit margin.

prediction.statement: The model's argmax matches the dataset answer on at least 98% of 200 prompts.
